thread:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a spike in NVMe metadata CRC errors in us-east1 scratchpool starting ~01:15 UTC. janitor.service is crashing with a SIGSEGV and leaving tempfiles around. GPU attach failures up ~3% as nodes are hitting ephemeral exhaustion.
priya: ugh. did you grab the janitor stack trace?
alex: yep, pasted the last few lines: ```Janitor[1423]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f3c... sp 00007ffd... error 4 in janitor_bin+0x1a3f
stack: janitor_free+0x4f, cleanup_tempfile+0x2b, process_dir+0x11c```
marco: any correlation with the nightly scrub window?
alex: scrub started 01:00, but this looks like janitor hitting a corrupted inode during cleanup. scrub-bot reports checksum mismatch on ~120 files in a single gnode.
jen: rolling GPU provisioning backlog now, ops team seeing queuing at the scheduler. can we throttle janitor or flip to safe-mode?
priya: agree, put janitor into read-only garbage-collection mode (don't unlink files) until we patch. that should stop new tempfiles being mishandled.
marco: +1. also schedule an immediate deep-scrub on the affected gnode; prefer a canary first to avoid mass IO spike.
samir: I'll open a ticket and escalate to firmware team in case it's HW. But logs suggest user-space segfault. tagging infra-oncall. @ops-bot can we lock down janitor deployment?
ops-bot: deploy lock engaged by samir at 01:23 UTC. Can confirm pause job applied to janitor fleet in us-east1.
alex: putting a short remediation runbook here: 1) pause janitor, 2) remount affected gnode read-only, 3) run checksum repair tool with --canary on 3 nodes, 4) after validation, run incremental unlinker with rate-limit, 5) deploy janitor patch.
jen: what about immediate capacity relief for GPU attaches? can we divert new requests to us-west while we triage?
priya: yes, smart-routing rule temp=true -> route us-east1 requests to us-west1 for non-data-local workloads. I'll push the route change (low risk)
marco: scrub-bot shows repaired 2/3 canaries succeeded, checksums consistent now. reading more, the segfault was in a path that assumes non-null xattr. patch is trivial (null-check).
samir: branch created, small patch + unit test. rolling a canary of janitor v2 to 5 hosts under 01:45 UTC. monitoring IO and attach success.
ops-bot: canary deployed to 5 hosts at 01:46 UTC.
alex: can confirm GPU attach errors dropped back to baseline after route shift and canary. tempfiles count decreasing on remounted nodes.
priya: after we validate, plan: 1) promote patch, 2) run controlled unlinker with concurrency=4, 3) run full scrub overnight with IO cap, 4) postmortem tomorrow.
jen: cost note — routing ~8% of load to us-west will increase egress by ~0.2% for the day. fine for now, call it out on the SRE runbook.
marco: +1 on postmortem. want to capture how janitor and scrub overlap can cause metadata thrash. maybe add a pre-check that pauses janitor during canary scrubs.
samir: will write the postmortem template and assign owners. current status: janitor patch promoted to canary succeeded, full rollout scheduled in 30m, scrub continuing under IO cap.
scrub-bot: report: canary-scrub nodes (3) -> no checksum mismatches, canary-unlink run completed successfully on 2/3, remaining node pending manual inspection.
alex: thumbs up. will update incident channel if anything regresses. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
